title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page opens section 1, 'A lemma of intersection theory', and serves as a foundation for the cases on the previous page (I–IV). Those cases ask when a homomorphism between Albanese/Picard-type abelian varieties ('lieux de VA') comes from an algebraic cycle on X×Y, and whether denominators are needed. That previous page makes the inversion of the map ψ_X depend on the 'th. de Lefschetz'.

Theorem 1.1 setup. X and Y are smooth, connected, projective varieties over an algebraically closed field k, of dimensions n and m. Z is an m-dimensional cycle on X×Y, i.e. of codimension n, so it is a correspondence from Y to X sending 0-cycles to 0-cycles. A_X and A_Y are the Albanese varieties (the abelian varieties, as opposed to the Albanese torsors A^1).

Theorem 1.1 statement. There is a unique homomorphism of abelian varieties u_Z : A_Y → A_X such that S_X(Z(𝔫)) = u_Z(S_Y(𝔫)). This holds for every degree-0 cycle 𝔫 on Y for which Z(𝔫) = pr_{1*}(Z · pr_2^*𝔫) is defined as a 0-cycle on X. Here S denotes the Albanese summation map. Moreover u_Z depends only on the numerical equivalence class of Z.

Corollary 1.2. If S_Y(𝔫) = 0 and Z(𝔫) is defined, then S_X(Z(𝔫)) = 0. In modern terms, correspondences preserve the Albanese kernel T(Y) → T(X).

Proof of uniqueness. There is a dense open U ⊂ Y such that Z(y) is defined for every y ∈ U(k), hence for every 0-cycle supported in U. A_Y(k) is generated by the S(𝔫) with 𝔫 of degree 0 supported in U. So u(k) is determined, and hence so is u.

Proof of existence (next page). Push Z forward to Z' on X'×Y, where X' = A^1_X is the Albanese torsor. Let B = Pic^0_{A_X}, the dual abelian variety. Intersect B×Z' with the Poincaré class Θ on B×X'. Push forward to B×Y to get a numerical class of divisors c on B×Y. Such a class defines a homomorphism B → Pic^0_Y, using the facts that numerical and algebraic equivalence of divisors agree up to torsion, and that homomorphisms of abelian varieties form a torsion-free group. The dual of this homomorphism is A_Y → A_X. This construction makes the dependence only on the numerical class evident.
errors: Corollary 1.2 is left grammatically unfinished: 'S_X(Z(𝔫))' with the conclusion '= 0' struck out and not rewritten. The intended statement is clearly S_X(Z(𝔫)) = 0, which follows immediately from Th. 1.1.
'u' is written for 'u_Z' in the displayed formula. Minor.

The claim that u_Z depends only on the numerical class is correct but non-trivial. It relies on Matsusaka's theorem (divisors: numerical ≡ algebraic modulo torsion) and on the torsion-freeness of Hom(A_Y, A_X). The page asserts it without proof; the next page supplies the mechanism.

ideas.what: A correspondence of the right dimension induces a homomorphism of Albanese varieties compatible with the summation maps, unique and determined on a dense open set.
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of the Albanese map under correspondences (action of CH^n(X×Y) on Alb)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as such; standard in Lang's Abelian Varieties and in motive literature (Murre, Scholl)

ideas.what: The induced homomorphism depends only on the numerical equivalence class of the correspondence, proved via the Poincaré divisor and divisorial correspondences on B×Y.
ideas.modern_name: Action of numerical motives on Albanese/Picard parts (h_1, h_{2d-1} motives); divisorial correspondences mod numerical equivalence = Hom of abelian varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil; Matsusaka; Murre (Picard and Albanese motives, 1990); Kleiman (1968), Scholl (1994)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Grothendieck's standard conjectures framework; explicit statements in Kleiman 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (1968) and Murre

ideas.what: Corollary: correspondences preserve the Albanese kernel.
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of the Albanese kernel T(X) ⊂ CH_0(X)_0

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but classical lemma: correspondences act on Albanese varieties, depending only on the numerical class. It is a preparatory step for the more interesting previous-page question of which homomorphisms between Albanese and intermediate-Albanese-type varieties are induced by cycles, a question tied to the Lefschetz standard conjecture. Nothing on this page itself is absent from the literature.
